learning_objective: 🎯 Master the structure of formal writing by learning how to present arguments, facts, and ideas in a clear, cohesive, and persuasive essay.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every essay must have three distinct parts: 1. Introduction (opens the topic), 2. Body Paragraphs (explains the ideas in detail), and 3. Conclusion (wraps up the essay).
Start with a 'hook' (a quote, question, or fact) to grab attention. End the introduction with a 'Thesis Statement'—one sentence that tells the reader exactly what the essay will prove or discuss.
Use the PEEL method for body paragraphs: Point (make a statement), Evidence (give a fact/example), Explanation (explain how it relates), Link (connect it to the next paragraph).
Paragraphs should not feel disconnected. Use transition words like 'Furthermore', 'On the other hand', 'Consequently', and 'In addition' to create a smooth flow of ideas.
Summarize your main points and restate your thesis in a new way. Never introduce brand new information in the conclusion. End with a strong final thought or a call to action.

fun_activity.title: 🍔 The Burger Paragraph
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a paragraph as a burger. The top bun is the Topic Sentence. The meat and cheese are your Facts and Details. The bottom bun is the Concluding Sentence. Write a 'Burger Paragraph' on why junk food is bad!

exam_tips: 📌 Always plan your essay before writing. Spend 3 minutes jotting down your points so your essay doesn't wander off-topic.
📌 Do not write one giant paragraph! Break your essay into at least 4-5 clear paragraphs.
📌 Avoid using casual language or slang (like 'gonna' or 'cool') in a formal essay.
quick_recap: ⭐ The introduction tells them what you are going to say, the body says it, and the conclusion tells them what you just said.
⭐ An essay should progress logically—usually from the most important point to the least important.
⭐ Strong vocabulary and correct grammar are just as important as good ideas.
